about_the_game:
You’re not just a cleaner. You’re an undercover agent, infiltrating the world of crime by posing as a cleaner, slowly collecting evidence against a mysterious hitman. The hitman runs a large organization called the syndicate who have bunch of cleaners, targets and hitmen.

Your goal is to catch the leader of the Syndicate by posting as one of the cleaners. The deeper you dig, the closer you get to uncovering how he operates—and how he does his assassinations.

The game has a scary layer. As you explore a crime scene, unsettling things could happen—shadows, whispers, apparitions. None of it is random. If you pay attention to the clues, you’ll understand why these things happen and how to survive them next time.

Here’s the part that gets sticky: You’re deep undercover.

Your mission: Infiltrate the Syndicate, a brutal underground organization led by the infamous hitman Victor Kane—a man responsible for Hundreds of kills, most of which were never supposed to be possible. The Syndicate doesn’t tolerate failure. And they definitely don’t tolerate rats.

Each dead body has a background story of their own and you can explore more around to gather evidence and know more about the dead. This will give you more information as to why hitman unalived this person. The more you explore, the more rewarding it is. We’re also adding a skill system—so over time you’ll unlock new abilities, making cleaning, investigating, and escaping from monsters more efficient.

And lastly, uncover the truth, because your decisions will alternate the storyline. The game offers multiple endings based on the decisions you make throughout the gameplay.

content_descriptors.notes:
Wiped Clean contains depictions of violent crime scenes with unsettling imagery, including blood and murder evidence. The storyline involves criminal activity, and an exploration of corruption. Sensitive topics such as betrayal, violence are part of the narrative.

There are NO depictions of sexual assault/non-consensual sex, BDSM, drug/alcohol abuse.. Viewer discretion is advised.
